 MANSHA SINGH & ORS. Petitioner(s)
VERSUS  STATE OF U.P. & ORS.
Respondent(s)
IA No. 63202/2025 - APPLICATION FOR VACATION OF INTERIM ORDER  Date : 08-04-2025
This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM : HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SANJAY KAROL  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SANDEEP MEHTA

For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Kavin Gulati, Sr. Adv.
 Mr. Rohit Amit Sthalekar, AOR  Mr. Dushyant Sharma, Adv.
 Mr. Mohith Sivakumar, Adv.
 Mr. Ajay Kumar Singh, Adv.
 Mr. Shashank Singh, Adv.

For Respondent(s) : Ms. Aishwarya Bhati, A.S.G.
 Ms. Poornima Singh, AOR  UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following  O R D E R 1.

It is not in dispute that the instant petitioners namely; Smt. Mansha Singh, Smt. Suchitra Singh and Smt. Pratima Singh are owners in possession of property viz., Municipal No./House No.D37/48A, Mohalla Badadeo, Ward Dashashwamedh,Varanasi.

Aggrieved by the fact that Mansha Singh vs State Of U.P on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28801806/
1 respondent No.4 namely; Varanasi Development Authority had initiated proceedings for demolition of the built up structure over the land in question, the instant petitioners preferred Writ Petition (C)
No.1514/2025 before the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad.

sentences.text: It is also not in dispute that there were five persons, who were occupying the property/built up structure as tenants, vacated the tenanted premises and the instant petitioners alone are being dispossessed.

Aggrieved of such facts,
the petitioners pressed for interim protection which was declined vide impugned order dated 20.01.2015 by the High Court which was not acceded to.
On 18.02.2025, this Court vide interim order had directed the parties to maintain status quo.
Respondent No.4-authority has filed counter affidavit as also an application seeking modification/ vacation of the order.

Yesterday when the matter was taken up, learned counsel for the parties were ad idem that if this Court were to exercise its power under Article 142 of the Constition with reference to Section 26 (1)(c) of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013,
the instant petitioners would be contemned in the receiving a total compensation of Rupees Seven Crores which would be the commercial circle/ market rate of the entire land i.e. 379 sq. meters and the remaining building/built up structure, if any.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Today, Ms. Aishwarya Bhati, learned Addl.

Solicitor General has placed on record communication dated 07.04.2025 which reads as under:
1. The compensation amount determined by the Honble Court in the concerned SLP shall be final, and upon its payment, ownership of the said site will be transferred to the State of the U.P., Housing and Urban Planning Department on an as is where is basis.
2.

Additionally, approximately 1000 sq. ft. of covered space for shops at the disputed site will be allotted to the petitioner on a priority basis, in accordance with the policy which would be set by (NHLML) National Highways Logistics Management Limited.

3. This SLP results in the disposal of the writ petition presently pending before the Honble High Court, Allahabad (Writ No1514/2025: Mansha Singh 7 2 others vs. State of UP and 5 others, and both the SLP and the writ Petition shall be disposed of in toto, unconditionally.

sentences.text:
3. Mr. Kavin Gulati, learned Senior Counsel, under instructions, submit that the instant petitioners are ready and willing to accept the aforesaid amount as total compensation for the consented acquisition in terms of Sections 26(1)(c) and 26(2)
read with Section 31 of the Act (supra).
Possession of the property already stands taken over by respondent-authority.

Ms. Bhati, learned Addl.
Solicitor General states that the entire compensation shall be paid to the petitioners either prior to or at the time of the registration of the sale deed.
The sale deed shall positively be got executed within next four weeks.
The expenses for registration of the document shall be borne by the respondent-authority.

The respondent-authority shall, in terms of the policy which would be formulated in future, abide by condition No.2 of the communication dated 07.04.2024 extracted supra.
4.
All proceedings inter se the parties including the Writ Petition shall stand closed.
We clarify that the compensation determined is in the peculiar facts of the instant case and shall not be a binding precedence.
Interim order(s) stands vacated.
5. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of.
6. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.

(VIJAY KUMAR) (ANU BHALLA)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS COURT MASTER (NSH)
